title: From Production Chemistry to Interfacial Reactions: Low- and Moderate-Temperature Biochar and Hydrochar for Integrated Wastewater Treatment
authors: B. Kayan and A. Alver · Reactions
abstract:
Low‐ and moderate‐temperature conversion can retain organic functionality and miner‐
al phases that influence contaminant uptake, but these properties do not establish dura‐
ble wastewater treatment performance. This critical review asks when production‐
dependent surface chemistry remains useful after modification, exposure to complex
water matrices, and regeneration. It prioritizes torrefied char and hydrochar prepared at
≤250 °C, compares materials prepared at >250–450 °C, and identifies higher temperature
derivatives by their complete preparation history. Evidence is evaluated through
matched preparation–property response comparisons, mechanism‐specific measure‐
ments, and treatment service outcomes. Low‐area hydrochars can remove metals and
organic solutes through contributions from accessible ligands, mineral reactions, and re‐
tained organic domains; pore development and greater carbonization can favor other
targets. These trends remain dependent on feedstock, pollutant speciation, and water
chemistry. High‐temperature activation can improve performance while changing the
material class and its resource requirements. Regeneration comparisons distinguish ca‐
pacity retention, pollutant recovery, sorbent loss, and residual stream treatment. Much
of the longer‐duration engineering evidence concerns higher temperature materials or
combined treatment systems, limiting direct transfer to unactivated low‐temperature
chars. Production costs and environmental inventories therefore require working capaci‐
ty, lifetime, and effluent quality data before they can support comparisons of equivalent
wastewater treatment services
